beats.title: Intro: One Side and an Angle
beats.says: Pythagoras needs two sides of a right-angled triangle. But what if you only know one side and an angle? That's what trigonometry is for, and by the end of this video, SOH CAH TOA will actually make sense.
beats.onScreen: Triangle diagram: angle 35°, hyp = 10 cm, opp = ?

beats.title: The Picture: Naming the Sides
beats.says: First, name the sides, starting from the angle you're using. The longest side, opposite the right angle, is still the hypotenuse. The side across from your angle is the opposite. And the side next to your angle is the adjacent.
beats.onScreen: Triangle diagram: angle θ, labels opposite, adjacent, hypotenuse
beats.key: Label from the angle: opposite is across from it, adjacent is next to it.

beats.title: The Picture: Same Angle, Same Shape
beats.says: Here's the big idea. Draw right-angled triangles with a 30 degree angle: small, medium, huge. The opposite side is always exactly half the hypotenuse. 1 out of 2, 2 out of 4, 4 out of 8. Same angle, same shape, so the ratio never changes.

beats.title: The Picture: That's All Sine Is
beats.says: That fixed ratio has a name. Opposite divided by hypotenuse is called the sine of the angle. So sine of 30 degrees is 0.5. Your calculator just remembers these ratios for every angle.
beats.onScreen: Worked: opp ÷ hyp = 0.5 // for every 30° triangle | sin 30° = 0.5 // that's all sine means | try it: sin 30 on your calculator

beats.title: The Method: SOH CAH TOA
beats.says: There are three of these ratios, and the way to remember them is soh-cah-toa. People say it like one word, soh-cah-toa, and that's what makes it stick. Sine is opposite over hypotenuse. Cos is adjacent over hypotenuse. And tan is opposite over adjacent.
beats.key: SOH CAH TOA: sin = O/H, cos = A/H, tan = O/A.

beats.title: The Method: Picking the Right One
beats.says: To pick the right one, ask two questions: which side do I know, and which side do I want? Here we know the hypotenuse and want the opposite. Cross out the adjacent: we don't need it. Opposite and hypotenuse: that's SOH, so we use sine.
beats.onScreen: SOHCAHTOA pick: know hyp, want opp
beats.key: Know one side, want another? The two sides tell you which ratio.

beats.title: Finding a Side: Multiply
beats.says: Let's finish it. The hypotenuse is 10, the angle is 35 degrees. Sine 35 equals opposite over 10. Times both sides by 10: the opposite is 10 times sine 35, which is 5.74 centimetres.
beats.onScreen: Triangle diagram: angle 35°, hyp = 10 cm, opp = ? | sin 35° = opp ÷ 10 // SOH | opp = 10 × sin 35° // times both sides by 10 | opp = 5.74 cm

beats.title: Finding a Side: Divide
beats.says: Sometimes the unknown ends up on the bottom. The adjacent is 8, the angle is 40 degrees, and we want the hypotenuse. That's CAH: cos 40 equals 8 over the hypotenuse. So divide: the hypotenuse is 8 divided by cos 40, which is 10.44 centimetres.
beats.onScreen: Triangle diagram: angle 40°, adj = 8 cm, hyp = ? | cos 40° = 8 ÷ hyp // CAH | hyp = 8 ÷ cos 40° // unknown on the bottom: divide | hyp = 10.44 cm

beats.title: Finding an Angle: Inverse
beats.says: To find an angle, use the inverse. The opposite is 5 and the adjacent is 7. That's TOA: tan of the angle is 5 over 7. Press shift, then tan, to undo it: the inverse tan of 5 over 7 is 35.5 degrees.
beats.onScreen: Triangle diagram: angle ?, opp = 5 cm, adj = 7 cm | tan θ = 5 ÷ 7 // TOA | θ = tan⁻¹(5 ÷ 7) // shift, then tan | θ = 35.5°
beats.key: Finding an angle? Use the inverse: sin⁻¹, cos⁻¹ or tan⁻¹.

beats.title: Calculator: Degrees Mode
beats.says: One calculator check before the exam: make sure it's in degrees. Look for a small D at the top of the screen. If it says R or G, your answers will all be wrong.
beats.onScreen: Worked: D on screen ✓ // degrees: correct | R or G on screen ✗ // radians or grads: wrong answers | sin 30 = 0.5 ✓ // quick test

beats.title: Exam Tips: Common Mistakes
beats.says: The mistakes that lose marks: labelling the sides from the wrong angle, multiplying when the unknown is on the bottom, forgetting to use the inverse for angles, and rounding too early.
beats.onScreen: Worked: ✗ labels from the wrong angle // start from your angle | ✗ 8 × cos 40° // unknown on the bottom: divide | ✗ θ = tan(5 ÷ 7) // angles need tan⁻¹ | ✓ label · pick · rearrange · calculate

beats.title: Your Turn: Question
beats.says: Your turn. The hypotenuse is 12 centimetres and the angle is 30 degrees. Find the opposite side. Pause the video and try it.
beats.onScreen: Your turn: question card with a countdown. Q: Hypotenuse 12 cm, angle 30°. Find the opposite side.
beats.question: Hypotenuse 12 cm, angle 30°. Find the opposite side

beats.title: Your Turn: Answer
beats.says: We know the hypotenuse and want the opposite, so it's SOH. The opposite is 12 times sine 30. Sine 30 is 0.5, so the answer is 6 centimetres. If you got that, you've got it.
beats.onScreen: Your turn: the answer A: opp = 6 cm.
beats.question: Hypotenuse 12 cm, angle 30°. Find the opposite side
